children: EUROPEAN STOCKS JOIN EURO LOWER, FRENCH BONDS SELL OFF
European shares are down in early trading, part of a broad cross-asset selloff that's seen the euro fall to its lowest in 16 months on the pound, and French spreads blow out again.
In terms of stock-specific developments, it's the chip complex that's underperforming. BE Semiconductor
down 3.3%, albeit after European tech stocks (.SX8P) hit a fresh all-time high on Tuesday.
The biggest gainer of the day is French car parts supplier Forvia
, up 7% after it signed a joint venture deal with Anand Group in India.
But generally we've been seeing selling across Europe. The STOXX 600 is down 0.3% and the blue chip Euro STOXX 50 index is down 0.8%.
The euro is also down 0.6% on the dollar and 0.3% on the pound, breaking out from the bottom of its range, and French 10-year yields are up 10 basis points.
